articles.title: Trump claims he predicted drops in oil prices, stock market and hits from Iran after Democratic win in midterm elections
articles.summary:
Trump claims he predicted drops in oil prices, stock market and hits from Iran after Democratic win in midterm elections

US president Donald Trump claimed that he predicted a stock market decline as well as harsher attacks from Iran after the Democratic victory in the recent midterm elections.

"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections. One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran... will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred," he wrote in a post on his platform Truth Social. 

Trump added that Iran "launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year," but claimed that the attacks have "all been knocked down, and done no damage".

"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won’t let that happen! Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," the American president further claimed. 

Trump went onto describe the elections as "very strange".

In another post, he questioned the drop in oil prices, saying: "Isn’t it interesting that Oil prices have dropped precipitously after the Midterm Elections? I said that was going to happen. The whole thing is a Giant Hoax!"

articles.title: Bahrain says Iranian strike wounds two, one critically
articles.summary:
Bahrain says Iranian strike wounds two, one critically

Bahrain said on Sunday that two people were wounded in an Iranian strike the previous day on “a civilian industrial site” in the Gulf kingdom, which has faced several attacks this week.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has repeatedly said they targeted US facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed earlier in November.

"In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain… a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded," Bahrain's interior ministry said on X.

"His condition is stable. A Pakistani resident was also wounded and is in critical condition."

Residents had seen smoke rising above Sitra Island, east of Manama, which hosts several industrial facilities, including a refinery operated by the state-owned oil company Bapco, AFP reported.

In a statement carried by Iranian state media on Saturday evening, the IRGC said they had attacked US Patriot air defence systems with missiles and drones at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, in response to the “continued violations of the airspace” of the Islamic Republic.

Bahrain's foreign ministry dismissed the IRGC's account, saying the site hit was purely civilian and industrial, calling the attack a direct danger to civilians and a violation of the kingdom's sovereignty.

Bahrain's neighbour Saudi Arabia on Sunday also condemned Tehran for its attacks on Gulf countries.

The Saudi foreign ministry expressed on X "the strongest condemnation and denunciation... of the criminal Iranian attacks against a civilian industrial facility in the brotherly Kingdom of Bahrain".

As a result of the heinous Iranian attacks on Bahrain yesterday, a Bahraini citizen with disabilities sustained injuries and is in stable condition, while a Pakistani resident was also injured and is in critical condition. Both are receiving treatment in the hospital. #Bahrain #MOI

— وزارة الداخلية - Ministry of Interior (@moi_bahrain) November 22, 2026
